current_claim: The repository is a self-describing, publishable, zero-maintenance toolbox with an honest catalogue and durable handoff.
mechanism: Repository conventions, root catalogue, continuity law, project-estate paths, and per-tool workflows jointly define what exists and how it survives.

findings.title: The estate map and the production tree are not held to one current machine-readable inventory.
findings.mechanism: README and CONTINUITY are manually maintained prose snapshots while additional top-level products and qualifications can appear without a corresponding estate-level release record.
findings.acceptance: One generated estate inventory enumerates every production surface, owner class, current head, qualification state, live-data dependencies, and unresolved backfill gate.

findings.title: Repository-wide design and interaction quality has no common acceptance floor.
findings.mechanism: Each tool can pass its own structural tests while typography, responsive behavior, role semantics, and visual fidelity regress independently.
findings.acceptance: Every public surface supplies visual goldens, typography metrics, interaction-delta tests, compact-width evidence, keyboard and touch coverage, and an explicit failure-state capture.

findings.title: The original zero-key invariant conflicts with the newly accepted live-provider architecture.
findings.mechanism: CONTINUITY prohibits keys and revocable services, while the current Manzanita successor deliberately supports optional Google, Mapillary, AirNow, and FIRMS adapters with explicit no-key fallbacks.
findings.acceptance: Record a constitutional amendment that permits bounded optional adapters only when billing, credential, storage, fallback, and source-custody behavior are explicit and a zero-key mode remains operational.

assets_required: root catalogue visual and accessibility goldens
constitutional amendment for optional live adapters
next_gate: Publish the estate inventory and make every prior completion claim subordinate to its backfill record.
